name: TekMedia
author: Tekzen

sections.description:
TekMedia adds the organisation and cleanup tools the WordPress media library is missing, without asking you to learn a second interface. It looks and behaves like wp-admin, because it is wp-admin.

Organise

  • Unlimited nested folders with drag-and-drop reordering
  • File shortcuts — put one file in several folders without a second copy on disk
  • Search across your whole library or inside one folder
  • Select many files at once to move or delete them
  • Replace a file while keeping its URL and attachment ID, so every post using it updates automatically
  • Import openly licensed photos from Openverse, Pexels or Unsplash straight into a folder

Optimise

  • Compress images on your own server — no account, no upload to a third party
  • 500 images a month on the free plan, with what is left shown before you start
  • Originals are kept, so any optimization can be undone
  • Filenames, URLs and attachment IDs never change

Clean up safely

  • Scan for files that no post, page, featured image or widget references
  • See exactly where a file is used before you touch it
  • Find duplicates — identical files, and the same photo re-uploaded at another size
  • Nothing is ever deleted without a confirmation that states the consequence in plain numbers
  • A recoverable trash: trashed files keep working on your site until you empty it
sections.faq:
Does the unused-media scan read page-builder layouts?

No. The free scan reads WordPress post content, featured images and widgets. Files used only inside Elementor, Divi, WPBakery, ACF or Beaver Builder may be flagged as unused, so check those layouts before deleting. Page-builder-aware scanning is a Pro feature.

Are my files deleted when I move them to the trash?

No. Moving a file to the TekMedia trash hides it from your library but leaves the file itself untouched, so any post using it keeps working. Files are only removed permanently when you empty the trash, or when the retention period you set in Settings expires.

What happens to my folders if I deactivate the plugin?

Nothing. Deactivating removes no data. Folder structure, trash contents and settings are all preserved, and only removed on uninstall if you have opted in under Settings.

Where does image optimization happen?

On your own server, using the image library PHP already has. Nothing is uploaded anywhere and no account is needed. That is also why there is a monthly allowance rather than a bill.

Will optimizing break the images already on my pages?

No. Optimizing rewrites the file in place, so the filename, the URL and the attachment ID all stay the same. If compressing a file would make it bigger — which happens with images that are already well compressed — it is left exactly as it was, and it does not use up part of your allowance.

Can I undo an optimization?

Yes, as long as “Keep original files” is on, which it is by default. Each optimized image has its original stored alongside, and Restore puts it back.

Is a shortcut a copy of the file?

No. A shortcut is a pointer, so it uses no extra storage. Deleting a shortcut removes only the pointer — the original file, and every other folder showing it, are untouched.

What happens to posts using a duplicate I trash?

They are rewritten to use the file you kept, before the copy is trashed. Featured images, images in content, gallery shortcodes and every generated size are all repointed, so nothing breaks. The copies go to the recoverable trash, not straight to deletion.

Do Pexels and Unsplash need an account?

Openverse does not, and it is the default. Pexels and Unsplash each need a free API key from their developer site, which you paste into Settings. Every imported photo has its credit and licence saved to the caption field automatically.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Added – Image optimization with a monthly allowance and restore.
  • Added – Bulk optimize and optimize on upload.
  • Added – Media usage tracking.
  • Added – Duplicate media detection.
  • Added – File shortcuts across folders.
  • Added – Stock photo import from Openverse, Pexels and Unsplash.
  • Improved – Trash and restore keep a file’s shortcuts.
  • Fix – Background jobs stalling after the first batch.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Unlimited nested folders with drag-and-drop nesting and reordering.
  • Grid and list views with folder-scoped search, file-type filtering and sorting.
  • Bulk selection that survives pagination, with move-to-folder and move-to-trash.
  • Drag files from your desktop onto the library to upload straight into the open folder.
  • Replace a file in place, keeping its URL and attachment ID so every post using it updates.
  • Unused-media scan that runs in the background and explains why each file was flagged.
  • Recoverable trash with per-file restore, restore all, and a retention period you choose.
  • Settings for the default view, sort, page size, upload destination, scan batch size and trash retention.
  • Full translation support and keyboard-accessible folder tree, tables and dialogs.

short_description: Organise your media library into folders, compress your images, find duplicates and unused files, and delete safely with a trash you can undo.
